Add a CI gate for pull request texts (#268)

Add tools/check-pr-text.py, a gate that checks a pull request
description and its committed squash-message file,
.github/squash/<number>.txt. In both texts it checks review-history
labels, through the label lint loaded by file path, em and en dashes,
-ise spellings whose -ize form is the standard one, an empty or blank
text, and a code fence that is opened and never closed. A blank text
holds nothing once whitespace, zero-width spaces, byte order marks and
HTML comments are removed. In the squash message it also checks line
width, revision ids and a subject that ends with the pull request
number. Fenced code, inline code, URLs and text between 2 double quote
marks on 1 line are masked from the label, dash and spelling checks; a
fence that is never closed masks the rest of the text and is reported
at its opener. A URL ends before an em or en dash, an unpaired
parenthesis or trailing punctuation, and the width check skips fenced
code and a line whose excess lies in 1 URL that reaches its end. The
gate finds the lint and the squash folder from its own path, makes no
git call, and exits 2 on unreadable input, on any other error it meets
and on a usage error, with the defect count as its last line. Its
inline-code scan takes time linear in the length of a line. Add its
suite, tools/test-check-pr-text.py, and the workflow
.github/workflows/pr-text.yml, which runs the gate on every pull
request with read-only permissions, keeps no credentials after
checkout and stops the job after 10 minutes. tools/ci-status.py does
not insist on the new check.

Residuals: a defect in a form the patterns miss, such as an upper-case
revision id or an -ise stem the denylist lacks; a defect inside a
masked region, such as an em dash inside double quotes, between 2 inch
marks or in the lines that an unclosed fence masks; a false failure on
honest text, such as code in an indented block, a list item or a
blockquote, a code span or a quotation that wraps a line, a URL in
angle brackets or backticks or followed by punctuation that runs past
72 characters, a line that combining marks push past 72 code points, a
hex run with digits and letters in a squash message, or a bare id of 1
or 2 capital letters and 1 or 2 digits; a message typed into the merge
dialog that differs from the committed file; and a description edited
after the last run.
